messages:
jordan: Quick Q — where's the per-pool autoscale graph for the eu-dedicated pool? Trying to correlate last night's latency spike with scale events.

maya: grafana -> Redwood Pools dashboard -> select cluster: eu-dedicated -> tab 'Autoscale events' should show scale up/down markers. here's a direct link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pools/eu-dedicated?panelId=12 (opens to the autoscale panel)

jordan: thanks — that panel shows a spike around 03:14 but I don't see a corresponding scale event. wondering which metric we consider canonical for triggering — cpu, queue_length, or kv_evictions?

lee: canonical signal is queue_length for the new autoscaler version, with CPU as fallback. kv_evictions are usually a downstream symptom (cache pressure) not a direct trigger.

sam: adding detail: the autoscaler rule is currently: if queue_length > 250 for 2m, scale up by 2 nodes; if CPU > 80% for 5m then scale up by 1. there's also a hard cap for bursts on eu-dedicated.

jordan: ah ok. what query shows queue_length? prom query?

maya: Prom: sum(rate(pool_queue_length_total{pool="eu-dedicated"}[30s])) by (pool)

maya: also useful (single stat): max_over_time(pool_queue_length_total{pool="eu-dedicated"}[5m])

lee: if you want traces for the requests that built up the queue, use the traces link from the dashboard (panel -> trace link). filter span.service=redwood-serving and pool=eu-dedicated.

jordan: copied. any suggestions on alert tuning? the pager fired twice last night but both were transient blips.

sam: we should widen the alert to 3m sustained and add a severity tier. proposal: P1 if queue_length > 500 for 5m, P2 if > 200 for 10m. that cuts noise from short spikes.

maya: agree. also add a mute-window for scheduled maintenance windows (we have a nightly patch at 03:00 in eu).

lee: FYI there's an existing alert rule file in infra/alerts/pools/eu-dedicated.json if you want to send a PR.

jordan: will do a quick PR. one more ask — is there a dashboard panel that overlays model fallback events (when requests were routed to a cheaper variant)? might explain latency changes.

maya: yes — Pool routing -> 'Fallbacks & routing' panel on the same dashboard. it logs last 24h fallbacks and reason tags (capacity|latency|policy).

ops-bot: Incident runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/pools-autoscale. Playbooks: check queue, check autoscale events, check model fallbacks, confirm KVS eviction rates.

jordan: great, thanks everyone. i'll open the PR for alert tune and attach the graphs. :thumbsup:

maya: ping me once PR is up, i'll review fast. :eyes:

lee: if you want me to post the adjusted thresholds to ops rotation, i can do that after PR merge.

jordan: thanks — will do.
